# **1  Executive Commitment**

## **1.1  Launch confirmation**

| UNQUALIFIED LAUNCH COMMITMENT Stupa confirms an unqualified commitment to an operations-ready athlete registration launch on 17 September 2026, using the production-proven OARS platform configured — not newly built — for Como Lake 2027\. No feature on the critical path to registration launch depends on unbuilt or bespoke development. |
| :---- |

This commitment is grounded in a platform already operating in production for 30+ leagues and federations across Europe, North America, Asia and Oceania, serving more than 20 million fans and players and having processed approximately 300,000 matches to date. The core launch scope in Section 5 (Phase A) uses standard and configured capability only; anything requiring third-party integration or a WMS/OC decision is identified in Appendix A and tracked to closure ahead of the 15–16 September 2026 UAT and readiness gate.

## **1.2  Solution summary**

Stupa proposes OARS (Online Athlete Registration System, powered by Stupa Events AI) as the single, hosted software service for Como Lake 2027: one governed participant record spanning identity, sport/event selection, Masters eligibility, teams, evidence, payments, accreditation, competition data, communications and reporting. Registration creates the authoritative entry record; the same record supports every downstream operational and Games-time process, reducing duplicate capture, manual reconciliation and rule drift between systems.

Stupa acts as prime contractor for the software service. The Organising Committee retains ownership of event operations and business decisions — sport rules, fees, participant outcomes, venue and helpdesk operations. Stupa's obligation is to make those operations possible through reliable, configured, monitored, tested and supported software, backed by named delivery and Games-time teams.

## **1.3  Key differentiators**

*What sets Stupa's proposal apart for Como Lake 2027 — one connected platform, open integration, Masters-specific configuration, single accountability, and delivery backed by a named team rather than software alone.*

| 01 ONE CONNECTED OPERATING ENVIRONMENT Identity, registration, teams, payments, accreditation, competition data, communications and reporting share a single governed source of truth with complete audit history, rather than a patchwork of point tools. | 02 INTEGRATION WITHOUT RE-PLATFORMING Documented APIs, webhooks and secure file exchange connect the event website, payment gateway, CRM, credential systems and sport-specific competition tools, so existing WMS/OC investments can remain in place. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **03** **A RULES ENGINE BUILT FOR MASTERS SPORT** Configurable by sport, discipline, event, category, team type, grade, venue, phase and effective date, with native support for youngest-member, average-age and aggregate-age team/crew/relay formulas (see Section 4.1). | **04** **SINGLE TECHNICAL ESCALATION POINT** Where an approved third party forms part of the solution (payment gateway, SMS/email, credential/access system), Stupa remains the single point of technical accountability and coordinates resolution. |

| 05  MANAGED DELIVERY, NOT SOFTWARE ALONE A named delivery team, 24/7 support model and an approximately 10–12-person on-ground Games-time team provide continuity from configuration through live event execution. |

# **3  Solution Architecture, Environments, Hosting and Roadmap**

## **3.1  Architecture principles**

* Multi-tier, fault-tolerant hosted architecture with separated production and non-production environments, infrastructure monitoring and controlled deployment (RFP NFR-01).

* **Configuration-first:** sport, fee, rule, quota, content and workflow changes are made through controlled configuration rather than bespoke code; every proposed custom component is disclosed in Appendix A (RFP NFR-04).

* Documented, versioned APIs, webhooks and secure batch exchange with sandbox credentials, rate limits and monitored retry/idempotency behaviour (RFP NFR-02).

* **End-to-end observability** across application, infrastructure, API, queue, payment and communication layers, with synthetic participant-journey monitoring (RFP NFR-06).

* Canonical timestamp storage with correct time-zone/DST handling and clear Europe/Rome display for event-facing users (RFP NFR-07).

*See Section 3.8 for the requirement-to-platform mapping, and Section 3.5 for how compliance responses are categorised.*

## **3.2  Environments**

| Environment | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| Production | Live participant and administrator service from registration launch through Games mode and closure. |
| Staging / UAT | WMS/OC acceptance testing against production-like data, integrations and configuration before each release. |
| Sandbox / integration test | API, webhook and file-exchange testing for the payment gateway, credential system, competition systems and other partners. |
| Disaster-recovery environment | Regional/site-level failover target supporting the RPO/RTO commitments in Section 6\. |

## **3.3  Hosting and data location**

| Hosting and subprocessor disclosure *Stupa hosts production data on a combination of Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) infrastructure, with the specific provider depending on the module concerned. Data is hosted within the EU/EEA (e.g., Frankfurt / Ireland regions) and, where GCP is used, geo-replicated across multiple EU regions. Stupa does not relocate production data outside the EU/EEA without the customer's prior written approval, save where required by law. Backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+), retained on a 35-day rolling basis (aligned with RFP Section 7.6), and supported by point-in-time recovery within that window. Stupa's India-based personnel may access EU-hosted servers only via secure VPN on a read-only basis; no personal data is stored outside Europe.* |
| :---- |

## **3.4  Standard vs custom map**

Appendix A identifies, requirement by requirement, whether Stupa's response is standard capability, configuration, a third-party integration, or partial (requiring confirmation or a specific evidence/design decision before unqualified acceptance). 

Across the 108 RFP Must/Should requirements addressed in this proposal:

* Comply – standard capability: used directly without bespoke development.

* Comply – configuration: existing capability configured for Como Lake 2027\.

* Comply – third party / integration: delivered through an approved external interface or provider.

* Partial: a named confirmation, evidence item or joint design decision is still required before unqualified acceptance — every such item is listed with its qualification in Appendix A.

No requirement in this proposal is answered as a Roadmap or Not available.

## **3.6  Illustrative participant and organiser journey**

The solution is built **around one connected journey**: registration creates the authoritative participant record, and every later step — team formation, evidence, payment, accreditation, competition and results — reads from and updates that same record. 

The table below **walks through the participant journey stage by stage** against the operational control each stage carries.

| Participant journey | Operational control |
| :---- | :---- |
| Create or claim an account | Identity, duplicate handling, consent and migration reconciliation. |
| Choose sports and events | Configured age/category rules, fees, quotas and schedule warnings. |
| Build or join a team | Invitations, rosters, roles, partner matching and revalidation. |
| Submit evidence and pay | Restricted review workflows, secure gateway integration, receipts and reconciliation. |
| Prepare and compete | Accreditation status, personalised schedules, updates, results and profiles. |

## **4.1  Masters-specific rule patterns**

Section 3 of the RFP sets out **nine Masters sport classification patterns** the rules engine must support. 

The table below maps each to Stupa's configuration approach and the operational control that governs it; representative scenarios are demonstrated live per RFP Section 9.3.

| Rule pattern | Configuration approach | Operational control |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Individual age bands | Sport-specific reference date, irregular/open-ended bands, date-of-birth derivation. | Boundary-date test pack and versioned rule approval. |
| Youngest-member teams | Real-time recalculation after roster change, with block/warning and retained prior decision. | Captain warning plus administrator override with reason. |
| Average-age crews | Included/excluded roles, decimal/rounding policy, substitution impact. | Crew calculation shown before confirmation. |
| Aggregate-age relays | Sum of member ages, band rules applied, revalidated on substitution. | Original and revised category retained. |
| Grades and multi-attribute eligibility | Self-declaration, evidence, automated screening, review/re-grade/appeal; age, weight, grade and membership combinations. | Sport-admin queue and complete decision audit. |
| Handicap and para classification | Issuing authority, index/value/class, validity, evidence, review, competition mapping. | Restricted access and separate retention for sensitive evidence. |
| Category combination | Combine competition fields without losing original award category or explanation. | Approval and publication history. |
| Exclusions and exceptions | Declarations/evidence, screening, reason-coded exception with dual approval for high-impact cases. | No silent reclassification. |

## 

| RULE AUTHORITY Stupa will not infer a rule where the website, sport guide and federation source differ.  The approved WMS/OC interpretation, effective date and version — recorded in the rule register — drives configuration and acceptance, consistent with RFP Appendix C3. |
| :---- |

## **4.2  Controlled rule-change workflow**

| Stage | Activity |
| :---- | :---- |
| 1 · Request | Record the proposed rule change and its source. |
| 2 · Impact | Identify affected entries, teams, fees, quotas and evidence. |
| 3 · Approve | Named WMS/OC owner confirms interpretation and effective date. |
| 4 · Configure | Apply and test versioned configuration with rollback evidence. |
| 5 · Communicate | Notify affected participants and retain the complete decision history. |

Stupa accepts **prime responsibility for the hosted software service**. The Organising Committee owns event operations and business decisions; Stupa delivers, configures, hosts and supports the software, trains OC users, monitors the service and resolves incidents. Stupa will name and mobilise: an executive sponsor, programme manager, solution lead, Masters sport/rules lead, data/integration lead, security/privacy lead, service delivery manager and Games-time software-service lead (named contacts at Section 2.4). 

Governance runs daily during mobilisation and launch, weekly through delivery and readiness, and daily again during Games mode, using a single RAID log, decision log, configuration register, requirements traceability matrix and release plan visible to WMS and the OC.

## **5.5  Launch acceptance criteria**

Launch acceptance follows RFP Section 6.4: all launch-scope Must requirements traced to UAT evidence with no open Severity 1/2 defect and no unapproved critical/high security finding; English and Italian journeys, including accessible keyboard/screen-reader paths, complete successfully; age/category, team, price, quota, document and payment boundary test packs pass; payment authorise/capture/fail/retry/refund/duplicate-callback cases reconcile; pre-registration migration reconciles with an approved rollback; load testing meets committed capacity and response targets; backup restore and launch rollback are demonstrated; and WMS and the OC complete a documented go/no-go decision, with any conditional acceptance carrying an owner, deadline and workaround.

## **5.6  Operations-ready gate before the Games**

No later than 30 days before the Games, and again before the Games change freeze, Stupa will evidence: final production configuration/data reconciliation; a successful end-to-end dress rehearsal; successful peak-load, failover, backup-restore, cyber-incident and loss-of-integration exercises; an approved service map, monitoring dashboards, escalation tree, RACI, duty roster and field-support deployment for Como, Lecco and Varese; approved SOPs and manual/offline fallbacks; training and competency evidence for OC users; and an approved change freeze and daily service-reporting format — per RFP Section 6.5.

# **6  Operations-Ready SLA Response and Support Model**

Stupa treats the SLA as a minimum contractual service schedule, not a statement of intent, consistent with RFP Section 7.1. It applies to the end-to-end Core Service, including Supplier-managed components and subcontractors; Stupa remains the single escalation point and does not stop SLA clocks while coordinating a third party. The full item-by-item SLA response, using the RFP's own Appendix B format, is at Appendix B.

## **6.1  Support coverage by service window**

| Service period | Coverage | How it operates |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Mobilisation and pre-launch | 24/7 critical-incident coverage; business-day delivery support; daily launch control. | Named programme and service leads; daily dependency, defect and readiness review. |
| Registration live | 24/7 critical coverage, extended around campaigns and deadlines. | Monitoring, on-call engineering, payment/integration oversight, participant-impact updates. |
| Games readiness (from 30 days before Games) | 24/7 critical and major coverage; extended all-severity hours. | Rehearsals, capacity/DR tests, service map, rota and venue fallback readiness. |
| Games mode | 24/7 all-severity command with agreed remote/on-site coverage. | Single command channel, incident commander, \~10–12-person team, daily reporting and integration monitoring. |
| Post-Games | 24/7 critical coverage; business-hours standard support through closure. | Finance/results reconciliation, export, archive, retention/deletion and transition. |

## **6.2  Availability commitments**

| Service | Standard target | Protected / Games target |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Participant registration, account and payment orchestration | ≥99.95% monthly | ≥99.99% monthly; no planned maintenance |
| Administrator, eligibility, team and finance workflows | ≥99.90% monthly | ≥99.95% monthly |
| Accreditation lookup/issue interfaces | ≥99.90% when enabled | ≥99.99% during published hours |
| Schedule/results publication and Supplier-managed interfaces | ≥99.90% when enabled | ≥99.95% during Games mode |

Availability is measured as the complete participant/administrator outcome, not infrastructure reachability alone, consistent with RFP Section 7.3. Unavailable minutes begin at the earlier of Stupa's monitoring detection or a WMS/OC report.

## **6.3  Incident severity and targets**

| Severity | Acknowledge (Protected/Games; otherwise) | Restore or safe workaround | Update cadence |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| S1 Critical | 5 min; 15 min | 30 min; 60 min | Every 15 min |
| S2 Major | 15 min; 30 min | 2 h; 4 h | Every 30 min |
| S3 Minor | 4 business h; 30 min in Games mode | 2 business days; same shift in Games mode | Daily / shift as agreed |
| S4 Request | 1 business day; 2 h in Games mode | Agreed fulfilment target / backlog | At status change |

## **6.4  Recovery, continuity and reporting**

| Commitment | Stupa response |
| :---- | :---- |
| Transactional RPO | ≤5 minutes for registration, payment status, roster and accreditation transaction data. |
| Core Service RTO | ≤60 minutes normally; ≤30 minutes during Protected/Games Windows, for a regional/site-level failure. |
| Backups | Encrypted point-in-time recovery plus daily backups; immutable/logically isolated copy; ≥35-day operational retention. |
| Restore testing | Quarterly sample restore/reconciliation; full pre-Games restore/failover exercise ≥60 days before Games mode. |
| Security incident notification | Within 2 hours of detecting a suspected material incident, with continuous coordinated updates. |
| Reporting | Live operational dashboard; monthly service report within 5 business days; daily launch/Games-mode report; weekly/monthly/daily/quarterly review cadence per RFP Section 7.8. |

## **6.5  Service credits**

Stupa accepts the RFP's minimum remedy model as the negotiation baseline (RFP Section 7.9): credits calculated against the monthly recurring Core Service and support fees for the affected service, capped at 25% per month, scaling from 5% for availability up to 0.10 points below target to 20% for shortfalls beyond 0.50 points, plus 2% per commenced 30-minute interval for a missed S1 restoration target, capped within the monthly total. Repeated Protected-Window or chronic failure triggers a mandatory executive remediation plan. Final measurement points, exclusions and remedies are recorded in the executed SLA schedule.

## **6.6  Incident, problem and communications management**

Monitoring or a user report opens the incident; critical and major cases are opened proactively rather than requiring the OC to prove an outage. A qualified responder takes ownership; S1/S2 incidents receive a named incident commander and shared bridge. Plain-language updates are issued at the agreed cadence without disclosing security-sensitive detail. An initial incident report is issued within 24 hours of restoration, with root-cause analysis within 5 business days for S1 and 10 business days for S2. Recurring incidents are tracked as problems; three similar S2 incidents within 30 days may be reclassified as an S1 problem requiring an executive corrective plan.

| Accessibility | Target WCAG 2.2 AA for participant and assisted-service journeys, validated through automated and manual review. |

| Integration and exit | Documented APIs/data flows, system-of-record mapping, transition support and deletion certification. |

## **7.3  Accessibility approach**

Participant-facing web and mobile journeys, the assisted-registration workflow, documents and communications are designed to conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA and applicable European accessibility requirements, tested through automated and manual review including keyboard-only operation, screen readers, zoom/reflow, focus order, error identification, accessible authentication, target size and colour contrast. The design also accounts for older users and people with changing vision, hearing, dexterity, memory or confidence: plain language, large usable targets, no unextendable time pressure, clear progress, save/resume and readily available human assistance. Accessibility and accommodation needs are captured separately from sport classification, with consent and restricted access. Critical barriers in the core registration path are treated as release blockers.

## **8.1  Total proposed value**

| TOTAL PROPOSED VALUE €88,000 excluding VAT — a one-time registration implementation fee, a 12-month platform licence paid quarterly in advance, and a defined Games-readiness/live-support fee.  Pass-through items (payment/gateway fees, SMS/email, identity/document verification, third-party licences, travel and accommodation) are additional and itemised below. |
| :---- |

| Component | Amount | Payment terms |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 · Registration implementation | €22,000 | €11,000 at contract;  €11,000 at registration production launch. |
| 2 ·\*Annual platform licence | €~~60,000~~ €40,000 for Year 1 | \*\*Four quarterly advance installments of €10,000 from September 2026 |
| 3 · Games readiness and live-event technical support | €26,000 | 50% at Games-support mobilisation; 50% within 10 days after event completion. |
| **Total excluding VAT** | €88,000 | Plus VAT, approved pass-through costs and travel per Section 8.2. |

**Important Notes:**  
*\*In recognition that Como Lake 2027 marks the first engagement between Stupa and World Masters Sport, and reflecting Stupa's commitment to building a long-term partnership beyond this event, the annual platform licence is offered at a discounted rate of €40,000 for Year 1, against a standard list price of €60,000. The total proposed value of €88,000 already reflects this discounted rate.*

*\*\*The annual platform licence starts from registration go-live on 17 September 2026, reflecting two decisions Stupa has made in this proposal: pricing registration and Games management as one unified project rather than two separately-charged phases (so only one one-time fee applies, not two), and not charging separately for the Como-specific customisation work this build requires, which Stupa would typically bill to other clients.*

**Scope of Each Fee Component**

*1 · Mobilisation and registration implementation includes:*

* White-labelled registration and games management platform, configured for Como Lake 2027  
* Dedicated EU-region infrastructure and database  
* Application design aligned to WMS/OC brand guidelines  
* Pre-registration data migration and reconciliation, where applicable  
* English/Italian localisation, with OC support

*2 · Annual platform licence includes:*

* Cloud hosting for the platform and a dedicated database  
* Infrastructure and maintenance support  
* Security and privacy maintenance, including database backups and security checks  
* Training and ongoing platform development  
* SLA-backed support (see Section 6\)  
* Usage allowance of 78,750,000 page requests/month and 15.90 TB storage/year; overage billed at USD 1.11 per 25,000 page requests and USD 0.36 per GB storage/year

*3 · Games readiness and live-event technical support includes:*

* Pre-Games dress rehearsals, load, security and DR testing  
* Named on-call and on-ground technical team (\~10–12 personnel) during the Games window  
* 24/7 incident monitoring and service coordination during Games mode  
* Post-Games reconciliation, closure and handover support

The proposed base fee is unchanged across the 7,500, 14,000 and 17,500 paid-athlete scenarios required at RFP Section 8.1, provided the agreed functional scope and service envelope remain unchanged and total traffic stays within the limit of 78,750,000 page requests/month and 15.90 TB storage/year. Usage-based gateway, messaging, identity and other third-party costs vary at provider actuals. The complete RFP-format pricing schedule (Appendix A2 columns) is at Appendix A.

The €26,000 Games-readiness and live-support fee covers the professional service effort of the agreed Stupa technical team; it does not include deployment cost. | **People** | Enhanced | Global 24/7 support across time zones, named roles and approximately 10–12 Games-time personnel. |
| **Continuity** | Accepted, subject to evidence schedule | RPO/RTO and restore exercises supported; detailed client-specific DR document to be attached. |
| **Security incident** | Accepted, subject to contract | Detection, two-hour material notification, evidence preservation and coordinated response. |
| **Reporting/governance** | Accepted | Live dashboard, daily/monthly reports, review cadence, problem management and improvement. |
| **Credits/remedies** | Subject to contract negotiation | RFP framework used as the negotiation baseline; measurement and exclusions to be finalised. |

| Backup architecture and DR position: Production infrastructure runs on a combination of AWS and GCP, with data hosted in the EU/EEA and geo-replicated across multiple EU regions where GCP is used. Backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+), and maintained as immutable, provider-managed snapshots protected by cloud-provider access controls and Stupa's internal permissions management, consistent with Stupa's standard continuity architecture. For Como Lake 2027, Stupa commits to the tiered recovery objectives set out in Section 6.4: RPO ≤5 minutes and RTO ≤60 minutes in normal operation, tightening to RTO ≤30 minutes during Protected and Games Windows, for registration, payment, roster and accreditation transaction data. Backups are retained for a minimum of 35 days on a rolling basis. Restore capability will be validated through quarterly sample restores plus a full pre-Games restore/failover exercise at least 60 days before Games mode, per Section 6.4. |

# **Appendix C — Value Beyond Software (Optional Digital Community Extensions)**

| OPTIONAL, NOT PART OF THE BASE €88,000 PROPOSAL The capabilities in this appendix are optional extensions to the mandatory RFP scope. They are not required for registration launch or Games operations and are priced separately if WMS/OC choose to pursue them — see the 'Optional modules' line in Appendix A2. |
| :---- |

The opportunity is larger than delivering a registration tool. Stupa's platform can connect the operational data created before and during the Games with services that strengthen participant engagement and create new digital value for WMS and the Organising Committee, should they wish to pursue it.

| Extension | Potential use |
| :---- | :---- |
| One connected operating environment | Participant identity, registration, teams, payments, accreditation, competition data, communications and reporting work from a governed source of truth — delivered as part of the base scope, not optional. |
| Integration without re-platforming | Documented APIs, webhooks and secure data exchange connect the event website, payment gateway, CRM, credential systems and sport-specific competition tools. |
| Monetisation opportunities (optional) | The same platform can support subscriptions, premium content, sponsor inventory, paid streaming, digital memberships and targeted offers, using consented participant and engagement data. |
| A lasting digital community (optional) | Player dashboards, personalised schedules and results, OTT, highlights, news and athlete stories can keep participants connected after the Games. |
| **Optional module** | **Potential use** |
| OTT and streaming | Owned live/on-demand destination and sponsor inventory. |
| Automated highlights | Scalable athlete, event and social video content. |
| Subscriptions and dashboards | Recurring access, personalised history and community growth. |
| Editorial and stories | News, case studies, athlete stories and Games legacy content. |

Stupa can also carry the platform from configuration and launch through operational readiness and Games-time technical delivery as a managed service, with a named service team, 24/7 support model and the approximately 10–12-person on-ground personnel described in Section 6 — this managed-delivery model is part of the base proposal, not an optional extension.
